title: Anchored baseline fee + ops-tier experiment for Private/VPC and on-prem packaging
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Objective: Run a two-arm pricing and entitlement experiment for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that reduces procurement friction while protecting revenue and upgrade cadence. Proposal is an 'anchored baseline fee' (annual) plus optional usage multiplier and three ops/support tiers. The baseline fee secures entitlement to product upgrades and audit-support windows; the usage multiplier accounts for sustained GPU or vCPU usage beyond the reserved bucket. Ops/support tiers (Standard, Enhanced, Enterprise) bundle distinct SLA windows, emergency patch SLAs, upgrade cadence guarantees, and included professional services credits.

Key design goals:
- Simplify procurement language for legal and procurement teams (one anchored fee + clear add-ons).
- Preserve predictable ARR for Redwood through minimum committed revenue.
- Make emergency fixes and upgrade assistance a clearly scoped add-on to avoid open-ended professional services.
- Offer upgrade cadence choices: quarterly opt-in, biannual standard, annual long-cycle for constrained customers.
- Surface clear KMS/HSM and audit log retention entitlements per tier.

Proposed components:
1) Anchored baseline fee: annual, non-refundable, includes entitlement to security patches and minor upgrades, base audit log retention (90 days). Anchored fee brackets by org size and core vCPU/GPU baseline.
2) Usage multiplier: per-GB-GPU-hour or per-vCPU-hour multiplier after committed bucket. Discount tiers for multi-year commits.
3) Ops/Support tiers:
   - Standard: business-hours support, 48-hour SLA for critical incidents, quarterly upgrade window, 30 days audit retention.
   - Enhanced: 24x7 paging for critical incidents, 8-hour SLA, biannual upgrade window with one emergency patch per year, 365 days audit retention, 8 hours response for security questionnaire follow-ups.
   - Enterprise: 24x7 priority, 2-hour critical SLA, quarterly configurable upgrade windows, included up to 5 days of remote PS for major upgrades, on-prem hotfix hotpath.
4) Upgrade cadences: customers pick cadence at purchase; higher cadence increases baseline fee but reduces per-incident PS charges.
5) Add-ons: accelerated upgrade concierge, extended audit retention, air-gapped appliance support, prioritized security questionnaire turnaround.

Risk/trade-offs:
- Lower friction vs. flexibility: Anchored fee simplifies renewals but may lock customers into cadence they later want to change; need flexible conversion rules.
- Revenue predictability vs. growth capture: Usage multiplier complexity could deter smaller customers.
- Legal: Must align with existing enterprise contract templates and export controls for on-prem kits.

Success metrics:
- Conversion rate on private deals within 60 days of RFP receipt (+ target +10% vs baseline).
- Average contract size (ACV) uplift for customers selecting Enhanced/Enterprise tiers (+30% target).
- Decreased legal negotiation time (days between LOI and signed contract) by 20%.
- Number of tickets flagged for PS scope disputes < 5% of closed deals.

Next steps:
- Pull baseline usage buckets from revenue ops and infra telemetry (ENG input).
- Draft a sample term sheet and SOW language for each ops tier.
- Legal & Security run-through on SQ answers and export control clauses.
- Pilot with 4 mid-market customers (sales-led) and 2 enterprise pilots (AE-assisted).

Notes on differentiation from prior experiments: avoids "seatless" framing and replaces multi-tier commit bands with a clear anchored-fee + usage multiplier that is easier to show on procurement POs. Emphasizes explicit upgrade cadence choices and an ops-tier that bundles security questionnaire SLAs as a commercial feature.
